text:
jordan: Heads up — while triaging an unrelated error we found some debug logs from svc-auth that include full email addresses in stack traces for a subset of requests. Pinging @samira @priya @mike for scope + quick privacy check.

samira: Ugh. Can you paste an example snippet and say where those logs live (S3, local ephemeral, datadog)?

jordan: Snippet from S3 (sanitized):
```
2025-02-20T14:12:03Z ERROR auth.handler Failed to load profile for user {
  "user_id": "u_12abc",
  "user.email": "alice@example.com",
  "session_id": "s_9xx"
}
```
Logs are in s3://redwood-prod-logs/auth/2025/02/20/*.gz (access controlled). I did a quick grep to estimate:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-logs/auth/2025/02/20/ - | zgrep -E "user.email" | wc -l
# -> 124 matches
```
I haven't deduplicated unique emails yet.

priya: Thanks. First things first — we need scope (unique users affected), whether any token/SSN/PII aside from emails were in the same lines, and recommend mitigation. I'll loop in legal/comms if this looks > threshold.

mike: Can you run a uniq count? Also confirm logs retention/replication (any copies outside prod region?). I need that for access approval.
jordan: Running a quick pipeline now:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-logs/auth/2025/02/20/ - | zgrep -E "user.email" | sed -E "s/.*user.email\\": \\\"([^\\\"]+)\\\".*/\\1/" | sort -u | wc -l
# -> 9 unique emails
```
No other obvious PII keys in the same lines on cursory scan (no ssn/tokens). Some stack traces include IPs but those are internal ipv4s.

samira: Ok 9 is small but not zero. Priya — do we have an internal comms template for small-scope logging exposures? Legal threshold for required external notice?

priya: Legal's threshold is >100 unique customer accounts or if credentials were exposed. For <=10 and only emails, we typically do an internal memo + optional customer outreach if they ask. I'll still notify legal for sign-off.

alex (sec-bot): @jordan please file an incident ticket with label=privacy_exposure, severity=low, include S3 paths and the sample snippet.

jordan: Filed INC-2025-024 and added the S3 paths + the grep outputs.

mike: Short-term mitigation: disable debug-level logging for svc-auth and deploy a config change to strip user.email from structured logs (replace with hashed_user_id or omit). I'll open a PR for the change and a canary deploy to one region.

jordan: PR -> https://git.redwood/infr/auth-service/pulls/472 (wip) — includes a log-redaction helper that replaces emails with sha256(email) prefix: 'uid:sha256:aaaa...'.

samira: Can we rotate any related keys? Looks like only emails leaked, not tokens, so rotation not necessary. Confirmed?

priya: Confirmed from initial review: no tokens, no SSNs. Still waiting on legal sign-off for external comms. I'll ping legal now.

audit-bot: Access request log: jordan requested S3 listing for s3://redwood-prod-logs/auth/2025/02/20 at 1739123468. Request recorded.

mike: For deployment: I'll push the config change and enable a runtime redaction filter in the logging pipeline. ETA 40m. Will keep canary off for 10min then roll.

jordan: I also rotated access to the S3 prefix (removed some legacy read group) and limited to required service principals; recorded in the incident ticket.

priya: Legal reviewed — approved internal memo only; no customer-wide notice required. They asked we keep a note in the incident timeline. Comms doesn't want a customer email for now.

samira: Ok, please add a follow-up action to add a lint rule preventing logging of keys matching /(email|user.email|user_email)/ and add a test in CI. Also we should add a dashboard alert for sudden increases in structured log fields that match email regex.

mike: Created infra ticket and feature flag gating for the lint. Added a monitoring rule with a threshold of >50 email-field matches per minute.

jordan: All changes merged to main and canary is healthy. Final counts in ticket: 124 raw matches, 9 unique emails, no exports to other regions.

priya: Thanks all. I'll draft the internal memo and post to #security-comms for record. If legal changes their guidance we'll update customers.

alex (sec-bot): Incident INC-2025-024 created and labeled privacy_exposure. Severity set to LOW.

samira: Great work. Closing the loop: add this to next postmortem agenda for logging defaults and secure-by-default structured logging. :white_check_mark:
